states.lead: From 2003 Q1 to 2026 Q1, the share of cases that are a single person without children rose in both programs across Ontario: OW 49.5% → 69.7%, ODSP 76.4% → 81.1%. The gap between the programs went from 26.9 to 11.4 percentage points. It was smaller at the end than at the start in all 15 CMAs: by the most in Oshawa (36.0 → 12.0), by the least in Ottawa–Gatineau (24.6 → 14.8).
states.defTest: Each rule was run from every quarter from 2012 Q4 (the first with 10 years of data before it) to 2025 Q4, using only the data up to that quarter, and compared with what happened later. The "likely range" is the middle 80% of those past misses at the same distance ahead.
states.f1Title: Gap between the ODSP and OW single-person shares in each CMA at six key moments (2003 Q1, 2019 Q4, 2021 Q1, 2023 Q1, 2026 Q1, 2030 Q4)

card.name: Ottawa–Gatineau
card.sum: In 2003 Q1, Ottawa–Gatineau's gap was 24.6 pp: rank 13 of 15 (±0.0 pp since 2003 Q1).

states.f2Title: Ottawa–Gatineau: the gap every quarter, 2003 Q1 – 2026 Q1, and the three outlook rules to 2030 Q4
states.f2Read: Ottawa–Gatineau: 24.6 pp in 2003 Q1, 14.8 pp in 2026 Q1. For 2030 Q4 the rules give 13.6 (convergence), 14.8 (no change) and 16.1 pp (10-year trend); they differ by 2.5 pp.
states.skillNote: Average miss = mean of |actual gap − projected gap| over the 15 CMAs and every starting quarter from 2012 Q4 on, using only the data up to that quarter (750 projections 1 year ahead, 525 for 19 quarters ahead, the last starting in 2021 Q2). "Too low" means the rule projected a narrower gap than happened. Bold: the smallest miss 19 quarters ahead (convergence 2.58, no change 2.62, 10-year trend 5.85 to two decimals). "No change" is the yardstick: a rule that cannot clearly beat it adds little.
states.outTitle: Outlook for 2030 Q4, sorted by the convergence rule (likely range in brackets)
states.take: Narrower overall, with setbacks. In 2003 Q1, 12 of the 15 CMAs had a gap of 25 pp or more; in 2026 Q1, none did, and the widest gap was 14.8 pp (Ottawa–Gatineau). Against a year earlier, though, the gap widened in 15 of the 15 CMAs in 2021 Q1, the most of any quarter. On the convergence rule, the 2030 Q4 gaps would span 10.0–13.6 pp (2026 Q1: 9.1–14.8 pp); for one CMA the three rules differ by up to 4.4 pp (Toronto), a reminder that the outlook is a projection.
states.outCard:
About the outlook
Tested from 2012 Q4 on, 19 quarters ahead the rules missed by 2.6 pp (convergence), 2.6 pp (no change) and 5.8 pp (10-year trend) on average.
The rules know nothing about future policy, benefit rates, caseload growth or the economy; a change in either program would break them.
They disagree most for Toronto: 4.4 pp apart in 2030 Q4.
A projected gap is not a target, and a narrower gap does not mean that needs converged.
